title: SupportBee vs Help Scout — Jon Martin
seoTitle: SupportBee vs Help Scout for Small Support Teams
description: SupportBee and Help Scout compared for small support teams: per-seat prices, free plan and trial, help centers, and HubSpot integration.
dek: Two shared inbox tools compared for a small team that answers customers from one support address.
Prices and features below come from each vendor's own pages, checked on the date shown. The SupportBee link is an affiliate link.

blocks.html: This comparison is for a team of two to five people answering customer email together, choosing between {{link:supportbee}} and {{link:helpscout}}. Many of these teams also keep customers in {{link:hubspot}}.
Both turn a shared address into a queue with owners and statuses. They differ in price, how far they reach beyond email, and how they connect to the rest of your stack.
Choose SupportBee if you want a simple shared inbox and the lowest per-seat bill. Choose Help Scout if you want to start free and expect to add chat, SMS, or a HubSpot integration as you grow.
For three seats on annual billing, SupportBee Startup comes to about {{calc:supportbee_three}} a month.

SupportBee Startup is {{fact:supportbee.startup}}, and Enterprise is {{fact:supportbee.enterprise}}. Per SupportBee, {{fact:supportbee.annual}}. Plans include {{fact:supportbee.unlimited}}, and Startup comes with {{fact:supportbee.kb}}. There's {{fact:supportbee.trial}}.
It keeps to the essentials: a shared inbox, a knowledge base, and the controls a small team needs to stop double replies.
Help Scout has {{fact:helpscout.free}}. Standard is {{fact:helpscout.standard}}, with {{fact:helpscout.channels}}. Plus is {{fact:helpscout.plus}}, and it allows {{fact:helpscout.light_users}}.
Check the monthly and annual toggle on Help Scout's pricing page, since the figures above come from its default view.

sections.label: Fit for a small support team

blocks.html: If email is the only channel and the budget is tight, SupportBee's per-seat price is hard to beat.
If you want to start for nothing, or if sales needs support history in HubSpot later, Help Scout's free plan and Plus tier give you that path.
SupportBee's pricing page doesn't list a HubSpot integration, so check before you rely on one.
Help Scout's free plan has one inbox, and the HubSpot integration sits on Plus, not Standard.
Count replying seats, list your channels, and decide whether support history needs to be in HubSpot. Those three answers pick the tool.
Run the trial on your real support address for a week, with a rule for who owns new email.

closing: Pick SupportBee for a cheap, focused shared inbox and Help Scout for a free start with room to grow.
